MtGox Co., Ltd., 28 Feb 2014: it applied that day for civil rehabilitation at the Tokyo District Court; it had closed its site at noon on 25 Feb 2014 (Japan time); about 750,000 bitcoins deposited by users had disappeared.
CFTC complaint of 13 Dec 2022: on 10 Nov 2022 FTX and FTX US halted all trading and withdrawals; over $8 billion in customer deposits were missing.

Chainalysis: on-chain scam revenue at least $14bn in 2025 (Chainalysis says the figure could exceed $17bn as it identifies more illicit wallet addresses) after about $12bn in 2024 (revised); impersonation scams grew more than 1,400 % in 2025.
ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025), warning signs: "Unknown exchange platform."

ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025), romance investment scam: "You have been contacted on social media, dating apps, or phone/text by someone you have not met in real life. This person may engage in frequent, personal and romantic conversations, building trust using fake profiles. Gradually, they steer the conversation toward financial opportunities, claiming huge profits from crypto-investments and encouraging you to invest with promises of high returns and low risk."

ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025), impersonation scam: "you receive an unexpected direct message (DM) or an email from someone pretending to be a trusted contact (e.g., a crypto-exchange, wallet provider, IT support, or even a friend)."

ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025), warning signs: "A request to send or share private keys and seed phrases (list of words to access and recover your crypto wallet)."

ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025), warning signs: "A guaranteed fast and high return."; romance investment scam: "promises of high returns and low risk".

ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025), look-alike address: "Scammers can make fake wallet addresses appear in your transaction history by sending a tiny amount of crypto from a look-alike address to your wallet." "When you try to send crypto and copy the wrong address from your wallet history, you unknowingly send funds to the scammer's wallet."

ESAs factsheet "Crypto frauds & scams: stay alert and protect yourself" (15 Dec 2025): "Never share passwords, private keys, or seed phrases: Anyone with access to them can take control of your assets. Legitimate companies will never ask for your passwords or security codes by email, text, or phone." In its impersonation scam, someone "pretending to be a trusted contact (e.g., a crypto-exchange, wallet provider, IT support, or even a friend)" asks for "your seed phrase".

CoinGlass 2025 annual report (data from 1 Jan to 20 Nov 2025): on 10 Oct 2025, combined long and short liquidations exceeded $19 billion, far surpassing the single-day highs of all previous liquidation rounds.

Portugal taxed crypto gains from 1 Jan 2023 (28 %, 365-day exclusion; Lei 24-D/2022).
Germany raised the private-sales Freigrenze from €600 to €1,000 from tax year 2024 (Wachstumschancengesetz, BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 108).
Italy raised the substitute tax from 26 % to 33 % for gains from 1 Jan 2026 and removed the €2,000 threshold from 2025 (L. 207/2024); euro e-money tokens keep 26 % (L. 199/2025).
Belgium introduced a 10 % tax on gains on financial assets including crypto from 1 Jan 2026 (law of 6 Apr 2026, Moniteur belge 21 Apr 2026).

The UK cut the CGT annual exempt amount from £12,300 to £6,000 for 2023 to 2024 and to £3,000 for 2024 to 2025. From 30 Oct 2024 it raised individuals' main rates, which cover crypto disposals, from 10 % and 20 % to 18 % and 24 %.

Ireland's Budget 2027 cut CGT from 33 % to 31 % for most gains, on disposals from 7 Oct 2026, by Financial Resolution No. 3 of 6 Oct 2026, a Dáil resolution with temporary statutory effect. Section 36 of the Finance (No. 2) Bill 2026 would enact the cut (not enacted on 2 Nov 2026).

alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index: Bitcoin only, 0 to 100, daily data from 1 Feb 2018; 6 inputs as published: volatility 25 %, momentum and volume 25 %, social media 15 %, surveys 15 % (marked "currently paused", redistribution undisclosed), dominance 10 %, Google Trends 10 %. CoinMarketCap's index: launched 3 Aug 2023, 5 components, weights undisclosed ("a complex weighting system"). On 16 Oct 2026 they read 63 "Greed" and 50 "Neutral", 13 points apart on the same day.

FCA InvestSmart (updated 16 May 2025): "Many experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover your outgoings for between 3 and 6 months." BaFin: a rule of thumb of 3 months' income. The CFPB gives no number.

ESAs joint warning 17 Mar 2022: "Consumers face the very real possibility of losing all their invested money"; revised warning 6 Oct 2025: "You may lose a lot, or even all, of the money invested", MiCA protections "not as extensive as those applicable to more traditional financial products (e.g. you will not benefit from compensation schemes)". MiCA Art. 6(5): the asset "may lose its value in part or in full", "may not be liquid", not covered by investor-compensation or deposit-guarantee schemes. FCA COBS 4.12A.11R: "Don't invest unless you're prepared to lose all the money you invest. This is a high-risk investment and you should not expect to be protected if something goes wrong." Central Bank of Ireland: "Consumers could face the possibility of losing all their money if they buy crypto".
